examples.text: In 2025, China had GDP per capita of 25,067 (constant 2021 international dollars, PPP), ranking 71 of 185 countries with data.
From 1990 to 2025, China's GDP per capita (PPP) grew 7.7% per year, against a median of 1.6% across 178 countries observed in both years.
From 2000 to 2025, China's GDP per capita (PPP) grew 7.3% per year, against a median of 1.8% across 182 countries observed in both years.
From 2010 to 2025, China's GDP per capita (PPP) grew 5.8% per year, against a median of 1.6% across 184 countries observed in both years.
With GDP per capita (PPP) in 2000 set to 100, China stood at 617 in 2025.

Since 2000, China's growth differs from what the cross-country line predicts for its starting income (slope -0.403) by +4.9 percentage points per year, where positive means faster. This is a descriptive residual, not a causal effect.
Agriculture's share of value added moved from 14.5% in 2000 to 6.7% in 2025; industry from 45.1% to 35.6%; services from 40.4% to 57.7%.
Median consumer-price inflation in China over 2014 to 2023 was 1.9% a year, with a peak of 2.9% in 2019.
Exports plus imports of goods and services were 38.0% of China's GDP in 2024, ranking 159 of 172 countries with data.
China's coarse export concentration index across five broad merchandise groups was 0.88 in 2022 (0.2 means evenly spread, 1 means a single group). It understates product-level concentration.

On standardized indicators China falls in peer group 2 of 3, a group of 60 countries whose average profile is high industry share, high inflation. Individual members can differ from that average; peer groups are descriptive, not causal.
